extracted.intended_audience: journal peer reviewers / researchers who perform manuscript reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for researchers serving as journal peer reviewers on how to perform timely, constructive, and community-minded manuscript reviews. Covers professional conduct, scope compliance, mentoring-oriented feedback, and recognition of reviewing work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mind the Time
rubrics_metrics.description: Respect deadlines; be prompt in responding to review invitations and notifications; request extensions immediately if needed; decline rather than miss deadlines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly to notifications rather than delaying. If you cannot complete the review on time, request an extension immediately; if you cannot responsibly complete it at all, decline the invitation rather than missing the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Intentional
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach reviews with a genuine desire to improve the work and provide valuable feedback even when the paper isn't ready for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on evaluating research quality rather than performing copyediting. Aim to give substantive, improvement-oriented comments that help authors move the manuscript forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read Guidelines and Scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Study the journal's reviewer guidelines and understand the journal's mission and scope before reviewing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the journal's reviewer guidelines prior to submitting your review; if no guidance is available, ask the editor. Use scope and mission to frame recommendations about suitability for the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educate and Grow Your Community
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat peer review as peer mentoring: provide detailed, specific feedback that educates authors and strengthens the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame rejections constructively to promote growth. Offer clear, actionable suggestions and explanations so authors (especially early-career researchers) can learn and improve their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Say No and Recommend Others
rubrics_metrics.description: Decline review invitations you cannot handle responsibly, and when declining, suggest suitable alternative reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unable to review, recommend colleagues, promising students, or postdocs to the editor as alternatives. Be proactive in suggesting replacements rather than leaving the editor to find new reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Bold and Constructive
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat all authors as intellectual peers regardless of credentials; give honest but respectful critiques and avoid dogmatic or rude language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dismissive or rude statements; apply the 'golden rule' to feedback. Be willing to make strong, clear recommendations while remaining constructive and professional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Get Credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Record and get recognition for reviewing activity through services and identifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register with Publons (now Web of Science Reviewer Recognition) to track contributions, connect reviews to your ORCID, and request formal credit records from publishers when available.
